land.text: Beiping, which the Sui general Li Jing could not defend around the new year 619, and Yuyang

predecessors.note: Gao joined Ge Qian's rebels 'in or before 616' and besieged Beiping from 617; the Sui court itself ended in 618 (Cliopatria's Sui row runs to 627 as remnants).

land.text: Gao's Yan state in northern Hebei: 'his Yan state was also integrated into Tang'

successors.note: After Zhang Jinshu's coup in 624; Cliopatria's row runs to 625.

capitals.name: Yuyang (Ji County, Tianjin)
capitals.note: 'He set his capital at Yuyang' (infobox: Yuyang first, then Huairong). The page says he later made Huairong (Huailai) his capital after killing Gao Tansheng, but gives no year, so the map keeps Yuyang.

correction.text: the 623 shape taken back to 619: the page names Beiping and Yuyang (taken around the new year 619), Huairong and, in 620-621, Wei Prefecture as a Tang commandery, but gives no outline for 619-622

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Gao Kaidao row begins in 623 but the page has him Prince of Yan 'Around the new year 619'. The extent for 619-622 is the 623 shape (confidence low: no page gives a boundary).

correction.text: the shape unchanged for 623-624; the state ends in 624, when Zhang Jinshu's coup drove Gao to suicide and 'his Yan state was also integrated into Tang' (Transition page), so 625 belongs to the Tang

keyframe_review.note: 81,783 km2 for 623-625, bbox 115.5-122.6 E, 38.7-41.9 N (463 cells, almost wholly inside the Tang's 626 shape). The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is not possible; the one-year overshoot to 625 is the only fault found. The page: 'In 624, his general Zhang Jinshu started a coup and he ... committed suicide'.

region.text: northern Hebei: Beiping and Yuyang (the capital), with the region 'centering Huairong'; infobox 'Ruler of China (Northern Hebei)'

ledger.note: 619: Gao Kaidao declares himself Prince of Yan at Yuyang. 'He declared himself the Prince of Yan and changed the era name to show independence from Sui' (around the new year 619); 'He set his capital at Yuyang'; infobox: reign 618-624, era name Shixing. He later killed the monk Gao Tansheng (Prince of Qi), took his troops and 'made Huairong his capital' (no year given).

619: Gao takes Beiping from the Sui. 'In 617 ... Gao put Beiping under siege'; around the new year 619 Li Jing 'could not defend the city anymore' and 'Gao Kaidao was then able to capture Beiping'; he also captured Yuyang around 619. Both are Sui commandery seats; the page gives no boundary.

region.text: Gao Kaidao's Yan, in northern Hebei (Cliopatria row 623-625; the page gives no boundary)

ledger.note: 620: Gao Kaidao submits to the Tang. 'In 620, he briefly submitted to Emperor Gaozu of Tang and was bestowed the imperial surname of Li'; 'In winter 620, Emperor Gaozu of Tang commissioned Gao as the commandant at Wei Prefecture' and created him the Prince of Beiping. A vassal tint, rule 4; the mirror of the tang-dynasty 620 vassal_start.

621: Gao Kaidao rebels against the Tang. 'but in 621 he rebelled against Tang and reasserted independence'; in winter 621 he kept the supplies Li Yi sent, 'breaking off the relations with Li Yi and the Tang dynasty'. The mirror of the tang-dynasty 621 vassal_end.

region.text: Gao's Yan state in extreme northern Hebei

ledger.note: 624: Gao's Yan passes to the Tang. 'By 624 ... Gao, faced with a coup led by his subordinate Zhang Jinshu, committed suicide, and his Yan state was also integrated into Tang' (Transition page); the Gao Kaidao page: Zhang Jinshu 'surrendering to Tang'. Gao had submitted to the Tang in 620 (Prince of Beiping) and rebelled in 621; the vassal pair is in this ledger (620, 621) and in the tang-dynasty ledger.

region.text: the Yan state of Gao Kaidao

ledger.note: 624: Gao Kaidao dies and the Yan state ends. 'In 624, his general Zhang Jinshu started a coup and he, realizing that the coup was about to succeed, committed suicide'; Zhang 'massacred Gao's adopted sons and Zhang Junli' and surrendered to the Tang (spring 624; the page gives no month).

wars.name: Gao Kaidao's revolt against the Tang
wars.outcome: Gao rebelled in 621, allied himself with the Eastern Turks and Liu Heita, attacked Yi Prefecture (not taken) and, with Jiali Khan and Yuan Junzhang, Yanmen in spring 623 ('could not capture it'); he and the khan took Mayi, which the khan later returned to the Tang. Zhang Jinshu's coup of 624 ended his rule and the Yan state was integrated into the Tang.
wars.note: Empty zones: the page records no ground held beyond Mayi, which was returned; the lasting change is the end of the Yan state in 624 (ledger).

certainty.note: A warlord's realm in northern Hebei: the page names Beiping, Yuyang, Huairong and Wei Prefecture but no boundary; Cliopatria's shape is the only outline.

sources.title: Gao Kaidao
sources.note: Identity, Prince of Yan c. 619, capitals, Tang submission 620 and revolt 621, Eastern Turks 623, death 624; no area, no territory after his death. Re-opened in the repair for the 620 submission (winter 620, Prince of Beiping, Li surname) and the 621 rebellion.

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang
sources.note: Gao Kaidao among the rebel leaders of 617 in extreme northern Hebei; 'his Yan state was also integrated into Tang' by 624; the other warlords of the transition (also used by tang-dynasty).

notes:
Written by the ea-04-a research agent on 2026-10-19 from the two pages in sources[] (budget 1-2 pages). Type is rebel because the Transition page lists Gao Kaidao among the 'agrarian rebel' leaders who controlled territory by 617 and the Gao Kaidao page has him declaring independence from the Sui and later from the Tang; the map should draw him hatched (rule 5) in his own colour until he is crushed in 624.

Cliopatria row 'Gao Kaidao' 623-625 (one shape, 81,783 km2) against the pages: the state runs c. 619 (Prince of Yan around the new year 619; the infobox says 618-624) to 624, so the row starts four years late and ends one year late. The new keyframe gao-kaidao_619 extends the 623 shape back to 619 on no better evidence than the row itself.

Not settled: where Gao's realm ended (the pages name Beiping, Yuyang, Huairong, Wei Prefecture; Cliopatria's neighbours list shows Goguryeo within 25 km in 623-625, which the pages do not explain), when he moved the capital from Yuyang to Huairong, the year he killed Gao Tansheng, and what the Tang did with Beiping, Yuyang and Huairong after 624 (the page is silent; the Transition page says the Yan state 'was integrated into Tang'). The 620-621 submission to the Tang as Prince of Beiping is recorded as a vassal_start (620) and vassal_end (621) with counterpart tang-dynasty here and as the mirror pair in the tang-dynasty ledger (the pair was missing here until the review of 2026-10-19; the Gao Kaidao page was re-opened: 'In winter 620 ... commandant at Wei Prefecture', 'in 621 he rebelled against Tang and reasserted independence').

Gazetteer: Yuyang and Huairong are not place entries; the realm is named by Tangshan and Beijing radii (the gazetteer has both). The capital dot is placed at Ji County, Tianjin (117.41 E 40.05 N), the researcher's identification of Yuyang; the page gives no coordinates.
